name: gizza-ai/json-key-case-convert
summary: Rename every JSON key to camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case or SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE

tool.description: Rewrite every object key in a JSON document into one naming convention, leaving all values byte-identical. target_case is 'camel' (default), 'pascal', 'snake', 'kebab' or 'constant' (SCREAMING_SNAKE). Splitting is acronym-aware, so userID becomes user_id and HTTPResponse becomes httpResponse. Keys are renamed at every level including inside arrays unless recurse=false; leading sigils like _id and $schema survive unless preserve_prefix=false; preserve_keys lists exact key names to skip. indent is spaces per level (1-8, default 2) or 0 to minify. Invalid JSON is reported with line/column, and two keys that would collide after renaming are an error rather than a silent overwrite. Runs locally.

indent.description: Spaces of indentation per level (1-8) in the output. Use 0 to minify to a single compact line. Default 2.

json.description: The JSON text whose object keys should be renamed, e.g. {"user_id":1,"profile_data":{"first_name":"ada"}}. Values are never modified.

preserve_keys.description: Comma-separated exact key names to leave untouched, case-sensitive, e.g. 'Content-Type,_id'. Use it for header names and for objects whose keys are data (ids, dates). Default: none.

preserve_prefix.description: Keep a key's leading sigils and convert only the rest, so '_id' stays '_id' and '$schema_url' becomes '$schemaUrl'. Default true; set false to strip them ('_id' becomes 'id').

recurse.description: Rename keys at every nesting level, including objects inside arrays. Default true. Set false to rename only the outermost object's keys (for a root array, the keys of the objects directly inside it).

target_case.description: Naming convention for every rewritten key: 'camel' (userId, default), 'pascal' (UserId), 'snake' (user_id), 'kebab' (user-id) or 'constant' (SCREAMING_SNAKE, USER_ID).
